heroHeadline: DG ISPR Confirms Op Ghazab lil-Haq Ongoing on Marka-e-Haq Day; Pakistan Signals Conditional Pause, Rejects Civilian Casualty Claims
heroSubtitle: On Day 71 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq (May 7, 2026), Pakistan's DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry used the first anniversary of Operation Marka-e-Haq (the May 2025 India-Pakistan clash) to reaffirm that Ghazab lil-Haq remains active and fully operational. Flanked by senior Navy and Air Force officials, Chaudhry categorically rejected Taliban allegations of civilian casualties from the May 5 Dangam, Kunar strikes, and introduced a new strategic framing linking the Af-Pak operation to 'India-sponsored terror' using Afghan territory — a narrative aimed at consolidating domestic support and deflecting international criticism. Separately, Pakistani media outlet Abb Takk reported Pakistan is signalling a conditional willingness to extend its operational pause: no new cross-border strikes if Afghan territory is not used for TTP attacks and TTP is not permitted to regroup. No formal ceasefire has been declared, no Urumqi Round 2 date has been set, China has remained silent since the Dangam incident, and the Afghan Taliban has not publicly responded to Pakistan's conditional framing. The conflict remains at an acute impasse with diplomatic signals of a possible tactical de-escalation coexisting with Pakistan's confirmed continuation of military operations.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
